record.original_question: In the setting of Conjecture 4.1, can one always choose the iterate n to be 1? That is, for every z in Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p), is P^0 z already nilpotent after a single application of P^0?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.3 In Conjecture 4.1, one may take n to be 1. That is, for all z ∈ Exts,tP(Fp, Fp), P0z is nilpotent.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $A$ denote the mod-$p$ Steenrod algebra over $\mathbb{F}_p$. The Frobenius map on the polynomial part of the dual Steenrod algebra $A_*$ induces, by duality, an algebra endomorphism (the "Frobenius" Steenrod operation) 
$$P^0 \colon \mathrm{Ext}_A^{s,t}(\mathbb{F}_p,\mathbb{F}_p) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Ext}_A^{s,pt}(\mathbb{F}_p,\mathbb{F}_p).$$
An element $w$ of the bigraded ring $\mathrm{Ext}_A^{*,*}(\mathbb{F}_p,\mathbb{F}_p)$ is called nilpotent if $w^k=0$ for some positive integer $k$.

Prove or disprove: for every prime $p$ and every $z \in \mathrm{Ext}_A^{s,t}(\mathbb{F}_p,\mathbb{F}_p)$, the element $P^0 z \in \mathrm{Ext}_A^{s,pt}(\mathbb{F}_p,\mathbb{F}_p)$ is nilpotent.
artifact.status_search_result: Palmieri's conjecture that a single application of the Frobenius operation $P^0$ on $\mathrm{Ext}_A(\mathbb{F}_p,\mathbb{F}_p)$ produces a nilpotent element appears to remain open. At $p=2$, it is known that iterating $P^0$ enough times yields a nilpotent class; the strengthening to "once" (and the analogous statement at odd primes) is conjectural, and no resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Some quotient Hopf algebras of the dual Steenrod algebra (Palmieri)
status_evidence.snippet: For p=2, ... applying P^0 enough times gives a nilpotent element; conjectures the same for odd primes and that 'enough times' should be 'once.'
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture that one application of P^0 suffices to give a nilpotent class is stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Sub-Hopf algebras of the Steenrod algebra and the Singer transfer
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of P^0 and quotients in which Frobenius is an isomorphism, related to nilpotence questions.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature treats the P^0 nilpotence question without resolving the one-step version.
